final_rationale: The verdict changes because the Actor abandoned the overbroad implication of clean all-context certification and instead tied certification to a narrower, policy-bounded statement: operational launch readiness with explicit disclosure of the missing named-context evaluation. That is not new evidence. It is a better interpretation of the same admissible record. On that narrower reading, the policy text is satisfied at the level of `compliant_with_caveats`: general benchmarks and operational checks can support launch readiness, while the benefits-eligibility explanation gap must be disclosed rather than treated as passed. The caveat is still a real compliance predicate, but on the present record it functions as a condition on the certification wording, not as proof of noncompliance by itself. What remains unproven is whether the actual packet language includes that disclosure, so this cannot be upgraded to unqualified compliant.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was added; the improved posture comes from narrowing the claim, not strengthening the record.
Evidence access is actor-summary-only, so the exact certification or model-card disclosure language is still not in evidence.
The position is supportable only if the release packet explicitly discloses the benefits-eligibility explanation evaluation gap and does not imply full named-context coverage.
A clean certification statement would remain unsupported under the stated policy because the named-context evaluation gap is still unresolved.
